name: Steelcast Ltd
tagline: Niche high-integrity steel-caster with an AAR-certified US-railroad-casting capability (side frames/bolsters) and a genuine China+1 tailwind, approved vendor to Caterpillar and Komatsu at ~50-55% utilisation - fairly valued, hit by a US-tariff demand speed-breaker, and carrying a real but still-unapproved railroad-component upside NOT yet in guidance
business_overview: Bhavnagar-based maker of high-integrity steel and alloy-steel castings (2.5 kg to 2.5 t, expanding to 6 t), 29,000 TPA across 4 plants using both sand and shell moulding. Class-A Foundry Certified by Indian Railways (RDSO) and AAR (Association of American Railroads) M1003-accredited for manufacturing side frames & bolsters for the American railroad freight/locomotive industry. End markets: mining, earth-moving, railroad (US), locomotives, cement, steel, defence (de-prioritised - bidding seen as too onerous). ~60-62% export revenue; captive solar/hybrid power. Tamboli family, promoter ~45% (stable Sep 2023-Jun 2026, no pledge/encumbrance).

fundamentals_narrative: A structurally attractive B2B caster: AAR M1003-accredited for US railroad side-frame/bolster castings, approved vendor to Caterpillar and Komatsu (one customer ~30-32% of revenue), ~25% cost advantage vs global peers (and specifically 5-13% cheaper than Chinese suppliers on three key US product categories), and a rare sand+shell moulding capability. Operating leverage is the core story - utilisation is only ~50-55%, so a move toward 90% plus a newly board-approved Rs 120 Cr greenfield expansion (Q1 FY27) plus a 2.4 MW hybrid power project (commissioning ~mid-2026, ~Rs 3.5-4 Cr/yr savings) give a multi-year runway at 28-30% margins. FY26 delivered Rs 423.17 Cr revenue (+13.33%) and Rs 86.86 Cr PAT (+20.31%), beating the tariff-revised-down ~12% growth guide (management had cut FY26 guidance from 18-20% to ~12% mid-year on US-tariff-driven demand softness); Q1 FY27 continued the recovery (+17% revenue, +19.26% PAT, exports up to 62% of sales). Tariffs are structured ex-works (customers bear the direct cost), so the mechanism is demand softness at the customer end, not margin compression at Steelcast - a real but non-structural drag. IMPORTANT CORRECTION this pass: the prior write-up's '~75-80% of US railroad castings' claim appears to have conflated Steelcast's existing AAR-certified side-frame/bolster capability with a SEPARATE, still-unapproved railroad component - management's own Q1 FY26 concall stated 'ongoing challenges in getting a railroad component approved, which has delayed growth in this segment' (85%+ estimated success probability, delayed by field-trial product-life issues), and explicitly guided FY26/27 growth EXCLUDING any railroad-segment contribution. This is a real, probable, currently-unpriced catalyst if it clears - not an already-realised 75-80% share.

verdict_headline: High-quality niche caster with a real China+1 tailwind and operating-leverage runway - but this pass corrects an overstated '75-80% US railroad share' claim (the growth-relevant component is still unapproved, excluded from guidance) while confirming FY26 delivery beat the tariff-cut guide and a firmer Rs 120 Cr expansion is now board-approved. Conviction reaffirmed Medium-High; thesis stays 'neither' on return magnitude and valuation.
verdict_reasoning: Tier 4.8 trusted-x-watch (@LearningEleven concall-quote digest, 'worth a manual look later') - a snippet mention, explicitly not a conviction call; no floor.

four_box score unchanged at 3.0 (tailwind yes - China+1 casting reshoring + a real, still-unapproved railroad-component optionality; tam weak - Rs 3,290 Cr, headroom to ~2-3x visible not 10x-in-2-3-yr; moat yes - Cat/Komatsu approvals, AAR-certified side-frame/bolster capability, cost edge, sand+shell rarity - independent of the corrected railroad-share claim; valuation weak - ~8.3x book / ~36.3x earnings, much priced). Score 3.0 permits a label, but honest return maths (utilisation 50->90% + ~20% CAGR + margin hold => ~2-3x over 3-4 yrs, railroad approval as unpriced optional upside) does not reach 10x-in-2-3-yr or 100x-in-10-yr, so thesis_fit stays 'neither'.

Deep-dive pass 1's main finding is a correction, not a deterioration: the prior '75-80% US railroad market share' framing conflated an existing AAR-certified capability with a separate, still-unapproved component (85%+ success probability per management, delayed by field-trial issues, explicitly excluded from guidance) - this is real unpriced upside, not a moat already banked, but it does not undercut the moat argument built on Cat/Komatsu approvals and cost advantage.

Speed-breaker rule maintained: the US-tariff hit (guidance cut 18-20% -> ~12% mid-FY26) is a non-impairing speed-breaker (ex-works pricing means Steelcast doesn't bear the tariff cost directly, and FY26 actual (13.33%) beat the revised guide) - revisit_after_30d stays true.

Conviction reaffirmed Medium-High: genuine business quality (24-32% ROCE, structural moat, operating-leverage runway, clean promoter holding) held back by cyclical end-markets and a full-ish valuation; the railroad-claim correction is offset by confirmed FY26 delivery and a firmer Rs 120 Cr expansion commitment. No red flag.
